transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Lena Park (Redwood CSM); Sophie Lyons (Lyons Director of Eng); Mark Patel (VP Product); Aisha Rahman (Lyons Security); Ben Carter (DevOps); Tom Nguyen (SRE)

Summary: Renewal and expansion check-in. Discussed Dedicated capacity upgrade, EU region deployment, contract extension and pilot/benchmarks. Next steps agreed.

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, i see most folks are here, Sophie thanks for making time
[00:00:07] Sophie Lyons: yeah no problem, thanks Maya, quick note we have about 60 days before current contract lapses so keen to understand options
[00:00:15] Mark Patel: and want to be sure cost and latency trade offs are clear, especially for holiday peaks
[00:00:22] Maya Chen: absolutely, so agenda for today — quick recap of current usage, proposed Dedicated upgrade and multi-region, pricing options for extension, and then technical next steps for a eu-west-1 pilot
[00:00:33] Diego Alvarez: hi all, i'm Diego from Redwood infra team, i can cover the perf and benchmark side and walk through autoscaling and kv cache behavior
[00:00:40] Ben Carter: sounds good, we care a lot about tail latency and cost per 1M tokens, we ran some internal stuff on our in-house gpus and saw variance at peak
[00:00:50] Tom Nguyen: also curious about how KV cache is handled cross-region, and whether prefix caching will be preserved if we route to eu nodes
[00:00:58] Diego Alvarez: short answer: prefix/KV caching is supported, but cross-region cache warmup is a factor — you can pin regional Dedicated pools to avoid cold starts, or use smart routing with prefix-aware cache hints
[00:01:12] Aisha Rahman: from security, we need details on KMS, HSM integration and audit logs — where can we see SOC2 artifacts?
[00:01:20] Maya Chen: we can share SOC2 report, and our Private option supports customer-managed KMS in VPC/on-prem variants — i'll share the security pack after the call
[00:01:31] Sophie Lyons: great, can you also share the Dedicated SLOs and what the SLA would cover for eu-west-1?
[00:01:37] Lena Park: yes we'll include Dedicated capacity SLOs, uptime targets, latency SLO by model class and typical per-route latency percentiles

[00:02:00] -- Topics: current stack and constraints --
[00:02:05] Sophie Lyons: quick background: we run a mix of on-prem GPUs for sensitive workloads and hosted APIs for less-sensitive. Peak is around 10k qps aggregated across chat and embeddings during promo events, average is 1.2k qps
[00:02:22] Ben Carter: our burst pattern is spiky, and batching helps but at tail we see latency spikes up to 900ms end-to-end which is above our SLO
[00:02:33] Diego Alvarez: understood, that pattern maps well to Dedicated with reserved capacity plus burst pools. We can recommend GPU pool sizing and autoscale policies to keep tail below target
[00:02:44] Mark Patel: cost is a gating factor; what sort of % change should we expect moving to Dedicated?
[00:02:50] Maya Chen: depends on commit level; Dedicated yields better unit economics at sustained throughput. With a 12-month commit you'll see ~20-30% lower per-token cost vs on-demand hosted for similar latency SLOs

[00:03:30] -- Deep dive: Dedicated capacity options --
[00:03:35] Diego Alvarez: we have three profiles: reserved baseline (predictable throughput), reserved + autoscale for burst, and reserved + burst pool on a higher-cost burst tier. For Lyons' pattern i recommend a baseline sized for 70% of peak and autoscale for spikes
[00:03:53] Sophie Lyons: will that require changes to our infra? we use internal proxies and route traffic via our edge
[00:03:58] Diego Alvarez: minimal. routing is via standard API endpoints, you can set route policies in Redwood Console and enable smart routing so sensitive workloads can route to Private pools when needed
[00:04:10] Tom Nguyen: question — network egress from eu-west-1, any extra charges or data residency caveats?
[00:04:16] Maya Chen: egress follows cloud provider pricing, and for data residency we can ensure processing and storage remain in-region for eu-only workloads, that's part of the Private/VPC controls if you need strict residency

[00:04:45] -- Pricing and contract extension discussion --
[00:04:48] Mark Patel: okay timeline again — 60 days, we want to lock terms and maybe add an extra region, is there flexibility on mid-term upgrades?
[00:04:57] Maya Chen: yes, we can include upgrade windows and clear tiers. Typical approach: a base renewal for X tokens with optional add-on reserved vGPU pools by region. We'll send a revised commitment proposal with tiered pricing
[00:05:08] Diego Alvarez: also worth noting quantization and model variant choices can materially impact cost; i can run a cost/latency matrix for your top 5 prompts
[00:05:16] Ben Carter: that'd help, we saw a lot of difference between 8-bit quantized runs vs fp16 at scale

[00:05:40] -- Security & compliance --
[00:05:42] Aisha Rahman: we need to know where audit logs are retained, retention default, and whether we can ship to our SIEM via syslog or S3 bucket with encryption enforced
[00:05:51] Maya Chen: audits and request logs can be forwarded to your SIEM, retention windows are configurable (add-on), and we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; we'll include docs and an example runbook

[00:06:20] -- Pilot and benchmarking plan --
[00:06:25] Diego Alvarez: propose a 2-week pilot in eu-west-1 against a dedicated pool we provision for you. We'll run your traffic traces and synthetic bursts, measure p50/p95/p99, cold start behavior, and cost per 1M tokens. Need Ben to share traces
[00:06:37] Ben Carter: can do, i'll anonymize traces and include sample prompts and batching patterns
[00:06:41] Tom Nguyen: what's the expected time to provision eu-west Dedicated?
[00:06:45] Lena Park: typically 48-72 hours for initial pool provisioning in a new region, can be faster with priority for pilot customers

[00:07:10] -- Clarifications / misc --
[00:07:12] Sophie Lyons: when you say quantization recommendations, is that something you'd test on our models or generic guidance?
[00:07:18] Diego Alvarez: we can run model-specific quantization trials in the pilot if you provide model binaries or access; otherwise we give recommended profiles based on model family and prompt length distributions
[00:07:30] Mark Patel: any vendor lock-in concerns if we later want to bring models in-house?
[00:07:34] Maya Chen: our focus is portability — you can pin model versions and export logs/artifacts; Dedicated and Private allow more control. No gating on moving models, though of course operational differences apply

[00:08:00] -- Objections and tradeoffs --
[00:08:03] Ben Carter: main objection is cost predictability vs flexibility — we don't want to overcommit and pay for idle GPUs
[00:08:09] Maya Chen: fair. that's why we recommend mixed approach: baseline reserved for predictable load plus autoscale/burst pools; we can structure financial terms with ramp windows and credits for unused baseline in year one as a concession
[00:08:22] Sophie Lyons: we'd also like clear rollback/fallback — if Dedicated in eu has an incident can traffic route to hosted fallback in us-east until eu is healthy?
[00:08:31] Diego Alvarez: yes, smart routing and automatic fallback policies can route to compatible model variants in another region; of course there are data residency implications which we'd document and you'd sign off on

[00:09:05] -- Logistics and timeline recap --
[00:09:08] Maya Chen: recap: Lyons wants Dedicated baseline in eu-west-1, plus burst policy, 12-month extension with option to upgrade. Action items: (1) Maya to send revised proposal/tiers, (2) Diego to prepare benchmark checklist and perf tests, (3) Lyons to share traffic traces and SOC2/KMS info, (4) Redwood to provision pilot pool upon agreement
[00:09:29] Sophie Lyons: yep that's right, we'll aim to get traces and security docs by Friday
[00:09:34] Mark Patel: can you also include cost sensitivity analysis for different commit levels? we'll use that for finance approval
[00:09:40] Maya Chen: yes, i'll include a cost/latency matrix and example yearly TCO comparison

[00:10:00] -- Simulated perf notes from Diego (SE) --
[00:10:03] Diego Alvarez: log note: for Lyons' prompt distribution, 70% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 20% medium, 10% long, so batching will be effective. Recommend model family X-2-7B quantized to 8-bit for non-sensitive workloads to reduce cost; use fp16 for high-fidelity private workflows
[00:10:21] Ben Carter: ok that helps, curious about tokenization differences across model families and how that affects token counts
[00:10:25] Diego Alvarez: we'll include prompt-level tokenization analysis in the benchmark; small differences can change cost calculations materially

[00:11:00] -- Questions from Security --
[00:11:03] Aisha Rahman: one more on key management — if we use customer-managed KMS in the VPC, who has access to rotate keys and how do we surface that in audit logs?
[00:11:12] Maya Chen: customer retains key control; rotation is under your KMS policy, Redwood only receives encrypted blobs. We log key usage events in audit trail and can forward to your SIEM

[00:11:40] -- Pricing scenarios (high level) --
[00:11:43] Maya Chen: scenario A: 12-month commit 1 region baseline 70% peak — X price; scenario B: 12-month commit + eu add-on — slightly higher baseline but lower per-token with region-local pools; scenario C: 24-month with ramp — best unit economics. We'll put numbers in the revised proposal

[00:12:10] -- Minor transcription artifacts --
[00:12:13] Speaker 1: okay um yeah (laughs)
[00:12:15] Speaker 2: mm-hmm

[00:12:30] -- Wrap up and next steps --
[00:12:33] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, action items in the notes, we'll follow up with the security pack, Dedicated SLOs, and a proposal. Any final Qs?
[00:12:40] Sophie Lyons: nope, thanks all, appreciate the clarity
[00:12:43] Mark Patel: thanks folks
[00:12:45] Ben Carter: thanks
[00:12:47] -- End of recording (approx 45 minutes) --

Notes: some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (model names, internal acronyms). References: shared doc links to be sent after call: link to proposal (placeholder), link to security pack (placeholder), benchmark spreadsheet (placeholder).
